O*NET43-2011.00 centres on answering, routing, information and messaging on a telephone system. Engineering system design, telemarketing and administrative management each have independent outputs; using a telephone does not mean the same occupation.

Inputs are the caller's purpose, the extension directory, approved public material, message requirements and the organisation's operating procedures. Check the object and the permission first and do not fill missing information by guessing.
Asking and restating can clarify the name, department and purpose; the editorial suggestion is to confirm first whom you need to contact and not to ask for personal details unrelated to the task.
Outputs include accurate transfer, a message with the time noted, a call record and the handover status; connection, leaving a message and business resolution are recorded separately.

Some posts also handle visitors, meeting contact, mail and data entry. Duties follow the organisational division of work, and an occupational list does not mean everyone collects payments or does security work.

Alarm notifications and unusual calls are routed and referred to the responsible person under the organisation's trained procedure, and the switchboard cannot make its own technical diagnosis or guarantee a safety outcome.

Directory updates and equipment use require checking the version and the permission. If an extension fails, leave the problem and report it, and do not change the exchange system or service permissions without authorization.

At shift handover, write the unfinished messages, the people already contacted and the pending statuses clearly; material storage and external sharing follow organisational permission, and real call records are not put into public work.
